title: Two Fast-Charging EV Stations Proposed for Jacaman Road and San Bernardo Avenue
excerpt: Laredo's Metropolitan Planning Organization voted Wednesday to open a 10-day public comment period on two federally funded fast-charging stations for electric…
content:
Laredo's Metropolitan Planning Organization voted Wednesday to open a 10-day public comment period on two federally funded fast-charging stations for electric vehicles, one on Jacaman Road and one on San Bernardo Avenue.

The vote, taken Nov. 18, is a required step to add the two awarded projects to the area's Transportation Improvement Program. Until the projects are added to that program, construction cannot move forward.

Where and how much

The two projects are at 2414 Jacaman Road and 5920 San Bernardo Avenue, according to Juan S. Mendive, director of the Metropolitan Planning Organization. "They're requesting that we add these awarded projects in the Laredo-Webb County metropolitan planning area," Mendive said of the request before the board.

The Jacaman Road station would cost nearly $900,000. The San Bernardo Avenue station would cost nearly $800,000. The costs include five years of operation and maintenance.

The projects are federally funded through the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) grant program, so there is no impact to the local budget, according to the presentation to the planning organization.

Timeline and context

Work is expected to start in the 2027 fiscal year.

The Laredo stations are part of a much larger statewide buildout. The Texas Department of Transportation awarded $226 million in NEVI Phase II funds in October for 321 charging stations across Texas, most of them in metropolitan planning areas. Texas is set to receive $323 million under the NEVI program for fiscal years 2022 through 2026. As of November, Webb County has 22 public charging points at six locations, according to U.S. Department of Energy station data.

What is not yet public

The operator for each new station and the number of chargers at each site have not been announced. Residents who want to weigh in can do so during the 10-day comment period now underway.
